task_instance: In a fresh sample Node project (task-lib), start from an initial committed scaffold, then introduce a messy uncommitted working tree that mixes a refactor (extract validateTitle helper), a new feature (completeTask), its tests, and a docs update. Split that mess into atomic, conventionally-typed commits (refactor -> feat -> test -> docs), verifying the refactor is behavior-preserving before adding the feature, running tests and a secrets grep before each commit (pre-commit hygiene). Then cut a release: bump package.json from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 (minor, since the new feature is backward-compatible), write a human-readable CHANGELOG.md entry grouped under Added/Changed, commit it, and tag the release with an annotated git tag (v1.1.0) so the tag, changelog, and version file all agree.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/addyosmani__agent-skills__git-workflow-and-versioning. Built sample project (package.json, index.js, test.js, README.md, .gitignore) with initial commit c4778af. Created a mixed working-tree change (refactor + feature + tests + docs all at once) and split it into 4 atomic commits by staging intermediate file states: 138a7e3 'refactor: extract title validation into validateTitle helper' (verified old test.js still passed against the refactored index.js, confirming no behavior change), 976765a 'feat: add completeTask to mark a task as done', b70cd91 'test: add coverage for completeTask' (node test.js -> 'All tests passed'), 5816c83 'docs: document completeTask usage in README'. Ran a secrets grep (git diff --staged | grep -i 'password|secret|api_key|token') before the feature commit -> 'no secrets'. Final git log --oneline shows clean, single-purpose commits with conventional-commit type prefixes and working tree clean (git status --short empty). For the release: bumped package.json version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, wrote CHANGELOG.md with a curated '## [1.1.0] - 2026-09-27' entry under Added/Changed, committed as 763c9d4 'chore: release v1.1.0', then created annotated tag v1.1.0 (git tag -a v1.1.0 -m 'Release 1.1.0'). Verified with `git describe --tags` -> v1.1.0, `git tag --points-at HEAD` -> v1.1.0, and `git show v1.1.0 --stat` showing the release commit's CHANGELOG.md and package.json diff, so tag/version/changelog are consistent. Final `node test.js` run confirms the feature works end-to-end. No pushes, no remotes, no credentials, no MCP/connector tools were used.
